ko.text: The festival starts with all Must items
Quality at least 30 – no cutting corners on visitor safety

name: Confluence Festival
tagline: Stages and permits + app and campaign
scope: Permits and site build, band contracts, safety, a festival app, ticketing and a campaign.
intro: You're organizing the first Confluence music festival. In 12 weeks the gates open for 15,000 visitors.
predWorld: Permits from the authorities, stage construction, band contracts, a safety plan. Fixed deadlines and official approvals.
agileWorld: Festival app, ticketing, website and a social media campaign. Test, measure, adapt.

dependency.lock: Waiting for the approved site layout (predictive milestone)
dependency.hint: Site map is waiting for a predictive milestone: approved permits and site layout.

workstreams.name: Permits from authorities, health and fire departments
workstreams.why: Official processes have set deadlines and requirements. You can't iterate on them – they must be planned early and completely.

workstreams.name: Stage construction and sound equipment
workstreams.why: Physical construction with a fixed date and suppliers. Last-minute changes are expensive and dangerous.

workstreams.name: Band contracts (booking)
workstreams.why: Artist contracts are signed months ahead with fixed terms and dates.

workstreams.name: Safety plan and event staff
workstreams.why: The plan must be approved by the police and fire department. Clear requirements, fixed approval.

workstreams.name: Festival app (lineup, tickets)
workstreams.why: Features can be delivered gradually and tuned based on tester feedback.

workstreams.name: Social media campaign
workstreams.why: Only data will show what works. Short experiments, measurement and adaptation.

workstreams.name: Festival website
workstreams.why: Content and features are added continuously; the first version can go live early and then improve.

workstreams.name: Side program by fan vote
workstreams.why: The program takes shape gradually based on what fans want – classic iterative work.

milestones.name: Permits and layout
milestones.okText: The authorities approved the permits and the site layout. The digital team can build the map from sprint 3.
milestones.lateText: Approvals dragged on. The final layout – and so the map – won't come until sprint 4.

milestones.name: Stages and equipment
milestones.okText: The stages are up and the sound is checked. Bring on the dress rehearsal.
milestones.lateText: Stage construction fell behind. Penalties and nervous partners.

milestones.name: Festival opening
milestones.okText: The gates are open! Mobile tickets work, and so do the lineup and the map.
milestones.lateText: The festival started, but key features are missing:

events.title: Forecast: thunderstorms
events.text: The long-range forecast shows a high chance of thunderstorms on festival weekend. The risk is in the risk register.
events.lesson: Risks with a response plan and a reserve won't catch you off guard. The predictive and agile parts can each respond in their own way – and complement each other.

choices.text: Activate the response plan: roofing from the risk reserve + the digital team adds weather alerts to the backlog
choices.feedback: Partners appreciate the preparedness and visitors will hear about the weather in time.

choices.text: Hope the forecast is wrong
choices.feedback: Partners ask what the plan is. There isn't one.

choices.text: Move the festival back a week
choices.feedback: Every contract (bands, stages, permits) has to be redone. Very expensive.

choices.text: Rush-order roofing and pay for it outside the budget
choices.feedback: With no reserve, it's extra money – and last-minute suppliers charge more.

events.title: Headliner cancels
events.text: Five weeks before the festival, the headliner cancels due to illness.
events.lesson: The predictive part (contracts) and the agile part (communication, app) must respond to a crisis in a coordinated way. The agile team can get the change out to people within hours.

choices.text: Booking secures a replacement per the contract; the digital team quickly updates the lineup and campaign
choices.feedback: Fans heard about the change from you, replacement included. The wave of outrage quickly faded.

choices.text: Stay silent until the replacement is signed
choices.feedback: The news leaked on social media before you said a word. Fans are furious.

choices.text: Offer everyone a refund
choices.feedback: Fair to fans, but the budget took a heavy hit.

events.title: Fire department wants another exit
events.text: During an inspection, the fire department demands another emergency exit. Booths and the stage have to be rearranged.
events.lesson: Mandatory (regulatory) changes go through change control in the predictive part – and their impact must flow into the agile part too.

choices.text: Change control: adjust the layout, update the permits and hand the new map to the digital team
choices.feedback: The fix took a few days, but everything is approved and the app map matches reality.

choices.text: File an appeal and change nothing
choices.feedback: The appeal failed and you lost two weeks.

choices.text: Quietly adjust the layout without new approval
choices.feedback: It came out at the final site inspection. The event may be banned.

events.title: A video went viral
events.text: A short clip of the stage build hit a million views. The other planned campaign posts are performing terribly.
events.lesson: Agile marketing: measure, learn, adapt. The plan is a hypothesis; real-world data takes priority.

choices.text: Adapt the campaign: more behind-the-scenes content, fewer planned ads
choices.feedback: Ticket sales jumped and the campaign costs less than planned.

choices.text: Stick to the original campaign plan approved in January
choices.feedback: The plan is followed, but the opportunity flew by.

choices.text: Spend the entire remaining campaign budget promoting that one video
choices.feedback: The reach is huge, but there's no money left for the rest of the campaign.

events.title: Presale crashed
events.text: When ticket presale opened, the online store crashed under the load for two hours. Fans are angry.
events.lesson: An incident is a chance to improve the process. Non-functional requirements (performance, security) belong in the Definition of Done.

choices.text: Blameless retrospective + load tests in the Definition of Done
choices.feedback: Root cause found, tests in place. The second wave of presale went smoothly.

choices.text: Replace the developer who built the store
choices.feedback: The team is scared and the new person doesn't know the system. The cause remains.

choices.text: Buy bigger servers and leave it at that
choices.feedback: It helped this time, but nobody knows where the real limit is.

events.title: Partner wants a tent in the middle
events.text: The main partner wants its big tent right in the middle of the site. But the layout is already approved by the authorities.
events.lesson: Handle changes to an approved baseline through change control. Hybrid lets you look for compensation in the agile part, where changes are cheap.

choices.text: Change control: assess the impact on permits and offer the partner an alternative (visibility in the app)
choices.feedback: The tent stayed at the edge, but the partner has its own section in the app. Everyone's happy.

choices.text: Agree right away – the partner pays
choices.feedback: New layout approval and a site rebuild. An expensive favor.

choices.text: Refuse without discussion
choices.feedback: The layout is protected, but the partner is wondering whether to come back next year.

events.title: Not enough volunteers
events.text: Three weeks before the festival, half of the volunteer event staff are missing.
events.lesson: Quick experiments in the agile part can help solve a predictive-part problem – with a plan B just in case.

choices.text: The digital team launches a recruitment campaign; production reaches out to an agency in parallel as backup
choices.feedback: The campaign brought in 80% of the missing people. The agency only covers the rest.

choices.text: Wait, it'll sort itself out
choices.feedback: It didn't. The safety plan no longer matches reality.

choices.text: Just hire an expensive agency for everything
choices.feedback: Reliable, but expensive.
